## Paper

Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning in Sequential Social Dilemmas

## World

resource_island

## Institution

Sequential social-dilemma institutions across resource/public-goods worlds.

## Agent type

Deep MARL agents in temporally extended social dilemmas.

## Theoretical benchmark

Cooperation and defection emerge over time through spatial/temporal coordination, not one-shot payoffs only.

## Learning setup

Sequential interaction with resource dynamics, partial observability, and multi-agent learning.

## Metrics

Cooperation/trade/contribution, sustainability, welfare, survival, coordination failures, robustness.

## Main result

The experiments show that conflict can emerge from competition over shared resources, and the sequential nature of social dilemmas significantly affects cooperation. Policies learned by agents exhibit strategic intentions that align with cooperation or defection based on environmental factors like resource abundance.

## What they prove

The paper proves that sequential social dilemmas can be modeled as Markov games with social dilemma inequalities. It characterizes how learned behavior changes with environmental factors and shows how conflict arises from competition over shared resources.

## What they only simulate

The paper simulates the emergence of cooperation and defection in multi-agent environments but does not formally prove the optimality of the learned policies or their convergence properties.

## What they do NOT test

The paper does not test the robustness of the learned policies to adversarial or noisy environments. It also does not evaluate the generalization of the policies across different types of social dilemmas.

## What we need to reproduce

Frame failed trade/institution activation as coordination/exploration evidence and report attempts versus successes.

## How our project differs

The paper develops sequential social-dilemma framing. The repo applies a smaller version to Resource Island and Public Goods with explicit diagnostics.

## Implementation obligations

Attempt counters; success counters; inventory/block reasons; final-window welfare/survival; cross-mind ladder table.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

Resource Island P.6 full trade-attempt and success diagnostics; Public Goods full outputs.

## Failure modes to audit

Claiming strategic avoidance when agents never attempted the cooperative action; no attempt/block breakdown; no horizon/exploration caveat.

## Project code comparison

Compare Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning in Sequential Social Dilemmas to Resource Island cross-mind results. The safe thesis claim is coordination/exploration failure under current training, not proof that stronger agents reject trade.
